The Nordic Grid Authority said its winter reserve margin will stay near 12 percent into February. Officials called the figure comfortable rather than generous, and said no rolling outages are planned. The authority has spent three years adding battery storage across the region and now counts 4 gigawatts of it. Demand has risen faster than the forecast published last spring, mostly because of new data centre connections in the south. A spokesperson said a revised outlook would appear in March and would carry a longer horizon than usual. Analysts who follow the region said the margin leaves little room if a cold snap arrives early, though none of them expect outages before the spring thaw arrives.
